First, recall that:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}f(s) & =⟨{lim}_{s\to 0}{e}^{s},\,{lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{{s}^{2}-2}{s+6},\,{lim}_{s\to 0}{4}^{s}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

- For the first component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}{e}^{s} & ={e}^{0}=1\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{{s}^{2}-2}{s+6} & =\frac{{0}^{2}-2}{0+6} \\  & =\frac{-2}{6} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}{4}^{s} & ={4}^{0}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{s\to 0}f(s)=⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{3},\,1⟩.$

Finally, the limit of $‖f(s)‖$ as $s$ approaches $0$ is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}‖f(s)‖ & =‖{lim}_{s\to 0}f(s)‖ \\  & =‖⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{3},\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{9}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{19}{9}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{19}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
